Per the project's recorded convention, a release is cut by pushing a git tag. The tag format is `vYYYY.MM.N`, where `N` is the release counter within that month.

1. Pick the next tag. Today is 2026-10-01, so the first October release would be `v2026.10.1`. Run `git tag -l 'v2026.10.*'` to see which numbers are already used, then take the next one.
2. Tag the commit on `main` and push the tag:
   ```
   git tag v2026.10.1
   git push origin v2026.10.1
   ```
3. CI builds and publishes. Don't publish by hand.

The repo has no release script, CI config or release docs, so I couldn't check any of this against the code. It comes from a shared EngramDB memory written by a human. The memory doesn't say which branch to tag from or what checks to run first. Ask a maintainer if you need that.

I haven't created or pushed any tags.
